title.zh: 卷251 列傳三十八 图海 李之芳
title.en: Volume 251 Biographies 38: Tu Hai, Li Zhifang
title.raw: 卷251 列傳三十八 图海 李之芳

sentences.zh: 列傳三十八

translations.literal: Biographies 38.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 38.

sentences.zh: 圖海李之芳圖海，字麟洲，馬佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Tu Hai, Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, style name Linzhou, of the Majia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai and Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, whose style was Linzhou, belonged to the Majia clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父穆哈達，世居綏芬。

translations.literal: His father was Mu-hada; the family had long dwelt at Suifen.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Mu-hada, and the family had long lived at Suifen.

sentences.zh: 圖海自筆帖式歷國史院侍讀。

translations.literal: Tu Hai rose from clerk to reader in the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai advanced from clerk to reader in the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗幸南苑，負寶從，顧其舉止，以為非常人。

translations.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor once visited the Southern Park; Tu Hai carried the imperial seals in attendance. The emperor watched his bearing and thought him no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shunzhi Emperor once visited the Southern Park, Tu Hai attended carrying the imperial seals. The emperor noted his bearing and judged that he was no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 擢內秘書院學士，授拜他喇布勒哈番，遷弘文院大學士、議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to bachelor of the Inner Secretariat, granted the rank of baitalabule hašan, and transferred to grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and councilor of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bachelor of the Inner Secretariat, granted the rank of baitalabule hašan, and then appointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and councilor of state.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，加太子太保，攝刑部尚書事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acted as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he received the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and served as acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 與大學士巴哈納等同訂律例。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others he revised the legal code.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others, he helped revise the legal code.

sentences.zh: 侍衛阿拉那與公額爾克戴青兩家奴鬥於市，讞失實，坐欺罔，免死，削職。

translations.literal: When the household slaves of Bodyguard Alana and of Duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, his judgment did not match the facts; he was found guilty of deception, spared death, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When the household slaves of Bodyguard Alana and of Duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, his ruling did not accord with the facts. He was convicted of deception, spared execution, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，遺命起用。

translations.literal: When the Shunzhi Emperor died, his testamentary edict ordered Tu Hai restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shunzhi Emperor's death, his testamentary edict ordered Tu Hai restored to service.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，授正黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor acceded, Tu Hai was appointed commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne, Tu Hai was appointed commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 李自成餘眾郝搖旗、劉體純、李來亨嘯聚鄖、襄間。

translations.literal: Remnants of Li Zicheng's forces—Hao Yaoqi, Liu Tichun, and Li Laiheng—rallied between Yun and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants of Li Zicheng's army—Hao Yaoqi, Liu Tichun, and Li Laiheng—gathered and raided between Yun and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，命圖海為定西將軍，副靖西將軍都統穆里瑪，將禁旅，會湖廣、四川諸軍討之，屢破賊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, Tu Hai was appointed Pacifier of the West, assisting Pacifier of the West Banner Commander-in-Chief Muri-ma with the imperial guard, joining the armies of Huguang and Sichuan to suppress them, and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, Tu Hai was made Pacifier of the West. Serving under Pacifier of the West Banner Commander-in-Chief Muri-ma, he led the imperial guard and joined forces from Huguang and Sichuan against the rebels, winning repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 未幾，郝搖旗為副都統杜敏所擒，劉體純亦破滅，惟李來亨據茅麓山，恃險負固，圖海圍之，絕其外援。

translations.literal: Before long Hao Yaoqi was captured by Vice Commander-in-Chief Du Min, Liu Tichun was also destroyed, and only Li Laiheng held Maolu Mountain, relying on its terrain and stubbornly resisting. Tu Hai besieged him and cut off outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hao Yaoqi was captured by Vice Commander-in-Chief Du Min and Liu Tichun's force was wiped out. Only Li Laiheng held Maolu Mountain, trusting its defenses and refusing to yield. Tu Hai invested the position and severed all outside support.

sentences.zh: 來亨窮蹙，自焚死，其下以眾降。

translations.literal: Laiheng, driven to extremity, burned himself to death, and his followers surrendered with the whole force.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Laiheng set himself on fire and died; his followers then surrendered with their entire force.

sentences.zh: 執斬明新樂王及所署置官屬，俘三千餘以還。

translations.literal: He seized and executed the Ming Prince of Xinle and the officials Li had appointed, and returned with more than three thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed the Ming Prince of Xinle along with the officials Li had installed, then returned with more than three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為弘文院大學士，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again made grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and advanced to first-class adaha hašan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reappointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and promoted to first-class adaha hašan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以兼都統乞解機務，不許。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, citing his concurrent post as banner commander, he asked to be relieved of state affairs; the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved of ministerial duties on account of his concurrent command of the banner, but the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 九年，改中和殿大學士，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to grand secretary of the Hall of Central Harmony and concurrently served as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became grand secretary of the Hall of Central Harmony and concurrently held the post of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，平南王尚可喜請老。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, petitioned to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 七月，吳三桂繼之，實探朝旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wu Sangui followed suit, in fact to probe the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Sangui followed suit, in reality to test the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 廷議移籓狀，莫洛、米思翰、明珠等皆主如所請，惟圖海持不可。

translations.literal: At court the question of relocating the fiefs was debated; Moluo, Misihan, Mingzhu, and others all favored granting the requests, but only Tu Hai objected.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated the princes' requests to leave their fiefs, Moluo, Misihan, Mingzhu, and others all favored acceding to them; Tu Hai alone opposed the move.

sentences.zh: 上意決，遂黜圖海議。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was set, and Tu Hai's view was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already made up his mind, and Tu Hai's dissent was overruled.

sentences.zh: 三桂既反，命攝戶部，理餉運。

translations.literal: After Sangui rebelled, Tu Hai was ordered to act as head of the Ministry of Revenue and manage supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sangui had risen in rebellion, Tu Hai was ordered to act as head of the Ministry of Revenue and oversee the transport of provisions.

sentences.zh: 十四年，察哈爾布爾尼劫其父阿布柰以叛。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Chahar Bu'erni seized his father Abunai and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Chahar leader Bu'erni seized his father Abunai and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 命信郡王鄂扎為撫遠大將軍，圖海副之，討布爾尼。

translations.literal: Prince Xin Ezha was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, with Tu Hai as his deputy, to campaign against Bu'erni.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin of the Blood, Ezha, was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, with Tu Hai as deputy, to suppress Bu'erni.

sentences.zh: 時禁旅多調發，圖海請籍八旗家奴驍健者率以行，在路騷掠，一不問。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial guard had largely been deployed elsewhere. Tu Hai asked to register stalwart bondservants of the Eight Banners and lead them on campaign; on the march they plundered, and he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: With most of the imperial guard already deployed elsewhere, Tu Hai requested that stalwart bondservants from the Eight Banners be registered and marched with the army. They looted along the route, and he ignored every complaint.

sentences.zh: 至，下令曰：「察哈爾元裔，多珍寶，破之富且倍！」

translations.literal: On arrival he issued an order: "The Chahar are Yuan descendants and possess many treasures; defeat them and your wealth will more than double!"
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the front he issued an order: "The Chahar are descendants of the Yuan and hold great treasure—defeat them and your wealth will more than double!"

sentences.zh: 於是士卒奮勇，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Thereupon the soldiers fought with ardor, each man worth a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At that the troops fought with such ardor that each man seemed worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 戰於達祿，布爾尼設伏山谷，別以三千人來拒。

translations.literal: They fought at Dalu. Bu'erni set an ambush in the valleys and separately sent three thousand men to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalu, Bu'erni laid an ambush in the valleys and detached three thousand men to meet the attack.

sentences.zh: 既戰，伏發，土默特兵挫。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined the ambush struck, and the Tumed troops were thrown back.
translations.idiomatic: Once fighting began the ambush was sprung and the Tumed contingent was thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 圖海分兵迎擊，敵以四百騎繼進，力戰，覆其眾。

translations.literal: Tu Hai divided his force to meet the attack; the enemy sent four hundred horsemen in support, but after fierce fighting their whole body was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai detached troops to counterattack. The enemy sent four hundred horsemen in support, but after fierce fighting their entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼乃悉眾出，用火攻，圖海令嚴陣待，連擊大破之，招撫人戶一千三百餘。

translations.literal: Bu'erni then brought out his entire force and used fire attack. Tu Hai ordered the ranks held firm; after repeated blows he routed them completely and won over more than thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Bu'erni then committed his whole army and attacked with fire. Tu Hai held his lines firm, struck again and again, and routed the enemy completely, winning the submission of more than thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼以三十騎遁，科爾沁額駙沙津追斬之，察哈爾平。

translations.literal: Bu'erni fled with thirty horsemen; the Khorchin imperial son-in-law Shajin pursued and killed him, and the Chahar were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bu'erni escaped with thirty horsemen, but the Khorchin imperial son-in-law Shajin pursued and killed him, and the Chahar region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，聖祖禦南苑大紅門，行郊勞禮。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Kangxi Emperor proceeded to the Great Red Gate of the Southern Park and performed the suburban ceremony of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, the Kangxi Emperor went to the Great Red Gate of the Southern Park to perform the suburban ceremony welcoming the troops home.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was advanced to first-class ashan-i hašan.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recognized with promotion to first-class ashan-i hašan.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督王輔臣以平涼叛應三桂，定西大將軍貝勒董額督諸軍攻之，久未下。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled at Pingliang in support of Sangui. The Pacifier of the West, Prince Dong'e, directed the armies against him but could not take the city for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fuchen, provincial commander of Shaanxi, rebelled at Pingliang in support of Sangui. Prince Dong'e of the Blood, Pacifier of the West, directed the siege for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣王屏籓、吳之茂等犯秦、隴，欲與平涼合。

translations.literal: Sangui sent Wang Pingfan, Wu Zhimao, and others to invade Qin and Long, intending to join forces with Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui sent Wang Pingfan, Wu Zhimao, and others to strike into Qin and Long, aiming to link up with the Pingliang garrison.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以圖海為撫遠大將軍，八旗每佐領出護軍二名，率以往。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Tu Hai was made Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief; each company captain of the Eight Banners furnished two guardsmen, and he led them on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Tu Hai was appointed Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief. Each company captain of the Eight Banners supplied two guardsmen, and Tu Hai led them west.

sentences.zh: 臨發，上御太和殿賜敕印，命諸軍咸聽節制。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the emperor proceeded to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, bestowed the commission and seal, and ordered all armies to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, the emperor appeared in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, conferred the commission and seal, and ordered every army in the field to obey his command.

sentences.zh: 既至，明賞罰，申約束。

translations.literal: After he arrived he made rewards and punishments clear and enforced discipline.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the front he made rewards and punishments explicit and tightened discipline throughout the command.

sentences.zh: 諸將請乘勢攻城，圖海宣言曰：「仁義之師，先招撫，後攻伐。

translations.literal: The generals asked to press the attack on the city. Tu Hai proclaimed: "An army of benevolence and righteousness first offers surrender, then strikes.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged an immediate assault on the city. Tu Hai declared publicly: "A benevolent army wins men over before it fights.

sentences.zh: 今奉天威討叛豎，無慮不克。

translations.literal: Now, bearing Heaven's majesty to punish rebels, there is no doubt of victory.
translations.idiomatic: We march now under Heaven's mandate to punish rebels, and victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 顧城中生靈數十萬，覆巢之下，殺戮必多。

translations.literal: Yet within the city are several hundred thousand lives; when the nest is overturned, slaughter will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet several hundred thousand people live inside the walls; when the nest is overturned, the killing will be immense.

sentences.zh: 當體聖主好生之德，俟其向化。」

translations.literal: We should embody the sage ruler's love of life and wait for them to turn toward civilization."
translations.idiomatic: We ought to honor the sage emperor's love of life and wait until they submit of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 城中聞者，莫不感泣，思自拔。

translations.literal: Those within the city who heard this were all moved to tears and thought of extricating themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard this inside the city were moved to tears and began to think of surrender.

sentences.zh: 五月，奪虎山墩，虎山墩者，在平涼城北，高數十仞，賊守以精兵，通餉道。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they took Tiger Hill Redoubt. Tiger Hill Redoubt lies north of Pingliang city, rises several tens of ren, was held by elite rebel troops, and controlled the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they seized Tiger Hill Redoubt north of Pingliang—a height of several tens of ren held by elite rebel troops and guarding the supply line.

sentences.zh: 圖海曰：「此平涼咽喉也。」

translations.literal: Tu Hai said: "This is the throat of Pingliang."
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai said, "This is the throat of Pingliang."

sentences.zh: 率兵仰攻，賊萬餘列火器以拒師。

translations.literal: He led troops in an uphill assault; more than ten thousand rebels lined up firearms to resist the army.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men uphill; more than ten thousand rebels deployed firearms to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 圖海令兵更迭進，自巳至午，戰益力，遂奪而據之，發大砲攻城，城人洶懼。

translations.literal: Tu Hai ordered the troops to advance in relays from the si hour to the wu hour, fighting with growing force until they seized and held the position, then opened great cannon on the city, and the inhabitants were thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai sent his men forward in relays from mid-morning until noon, fighting with mounting fury until they took and held the redoubt. He then turned heavy cannon on the city, throwing the defenders into panic.

sentences.zh: 圖海用幕客周昌策，招輔臣降。

translations.literal: Tu Hai employed the plan of his retainer Zhou Chang to induce Fuchen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai followed a plan devised by his adviser Zhou Chang to win Fuchen's surrender.

sentences.zh: 昌，字培公，荊門諸生。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Peigong, was a licentiate of Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style was Peigong, was a licentiate of Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 好奇計。

translations.literal: He delighted in ingenious stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of bold stratagems.

sentences.zh: 佐振武將軍吳丹有勞，以七品官錄用。

translations.literal: For meritorious service assisting Pacifier of Martial Valor Wu Dan he was enrolled as a seventh-rank official.
translations.idiomatic: For distinguished service under Pacifier of Martial Valor Wu Dan he was enrolled as a seventh-rank official.

sentences.zh: 圖海次潼關，以策乾之，客諸幕。

translations.literal: When Tu Hai halted at Tong Pass he valued Chang's plans and kept him among his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Tu Hai encamped at Tong Pass he sought Chang's counsel and retained him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 輔臣所署置總兵黃九疇、布政使龔榮遇皆昌鄉人，屢勸輔臣反正，以蠟丸告昌，昌白圖海。

translations.literal: The regional commander Huang Jiuchou and the provincial administration commissioner Gong Rongyu, whom Fuchen had appointed, were both fellow townsmen of Chang. They repeatedly urged Fuchen to return to allegiance, sent word to Chang in wax pellets, and Chang reported this to Tu Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Huang Jiuchou and provincial administration commissioner Gong Rongyu, whom Fuchen had appointed, were both natives of Chang's home district. They repeatedly urged Fuchen to return to the Qing side, sent messages to Chang in wax pellets, and Chang informed Tu Hai.

sentences.zh: 圖海即令昌入城諭降，輔臣遣其將從昌出謁，圖海聞上，上許之。

translations.literal: Tu Hai at once ordered Chang into the city to urge surrender. Fuchen sent a general out with Chang to pay respects; Tu Hai reported to the throne, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai immediately sent Chang into the city to negotiate surrender. Fuchen dispatched a general with Chang to pay his respects; Tu Hai reported to the throne, and the emperor gave his consent.

sentences.zh: 乃假昌參議道，賚詔往撫。

translations.literal: Chang was then given the acting rank of participation commissioner and sent with an imperial edict to pacify Fuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was then given the acting rank of participation commissioner and sent with an imperial edict to win Fuchen over.

sentences.zh: 輔臣使榮遇上軍民冊，子繼貞繳三桂所授敕印，顧猶觀望，復命昌偕兄子保定諭之，乃薙發降。

translations.literal: Fuchen had Rongyu present the register of troops and civilians; his son Jizhen returned the commission and seal Sangui had granted. Yet he still hesitated, so Chang was again sent with his nephew Baoding to persuade him, and only then did he shave his head and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen had Rongyu submit the register of troops and civilians, and his son Jizhen returned the commission and seal Sangui had granted him. Still he wavered, so Chang was sent again with his nephew Baoding to persuade him, and only then did Fuchen shave his head and surrender.

sentences.zh: 因令吳丹入城撫定。

translations.literal: Tu Hai then ordered Wu Dan into the city to pacify and settle the population.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai then ordered Wu Dan into the city to restore order.

sentences.zh: 吳之茂聞平涼下，自秦州遁，遣將軍佛尼勒敗之於牡丹園，又敗之於西和縣北山。

translations.literal: When Wu Zhimao heard that Pingliang had fallen, he fled from Qinzhou. General Fonile was sent and defeated him at Mudan Garden and again on North Mountain in Xihe County.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Pingliang had fallen, Wu Zhimao fled from Qinzhou. General Fonile was dispatched, defeated him at Mudan Garden, and routed him again on North Mountain in Xihe County.

sentences.zh: 將軍穆佔進攻王屏籓於樂門，敗賊於紅崖，復禮縣。

translations.literal: General Muzhan advanced against Wang Pingfan at Lemen, defeated the rebels at Hongya, and recovered Li County.
translations.idiomatic: General Muzhan attacked Wang Pingfan at Lemen, defeated the rebels at Hongya, and recovered Li County.

sentences.zh: 輔臣所署置巡撫陳彭，總兵週養民、王好問等相繼降。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Chen Peng, regional commanders Zhou Yangmin and Wang Haowen, and others whom Fuchen had appointed surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governor Chen Peng, regional commanders Zhou Yangmin and Wang Haowen, and other officials Fuchen had appointed surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 秦地略定。

translations.literal: The Qin region was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin region was largely brought under control.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進三等公，世襲。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded; he was advanced to third-rank duke with hereditary entitlement.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recognized with promotion to third-rank duke, inheritable by his descendants.

sentences.zh: 圖海疏請遣兵赴湖廣，會徵三桂，上命圖海親率精銳以行。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized asking to send troops to Huguang to join the campaign against Sangui. The emperor ordered Tu Hai personally to lead picked troops thither.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai memorialized requesting troops for Huguang to join the campaign against Sangui. The emperor ordered him to lead elite forces there in person.

sentences.zh: 圖海疏陳陝西初定、反側未安狀，乃授穆佔征南將軍，率滿洲兵及平涼降卒往，圖海仍留鎮。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized that Shaanxi had only just been pacified and disaffection was not yet settled, whereupon Muzhan was made Southern Campaign General to lead Manchu troops and Pingliang surrender troops thither, while Tu Hai remained to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai explained in a memorial that Shaanxi had only just been pacified and loyalties were still unsettled. Muzhan was therefore made Southern Campaign General and sent with Manchu troops and Pingliang surrender troops, while Tu Hai remained to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 時平涼、慶陽雖下，漢中、興安猶為賊據。

translations.literal: At the time, though Pingliang and Qingyang had fallen, Hanzhong and Xing'an were still held by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Although Pingliang and Qingyang had been recovered, Hanzhong and Xing'an were still in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 圖海奏調綠旗兵，期明年正月檄提督孫思克赴秦州，趙良棟赴鳳翔，與張勇、王進寶會師進取，勇等謂須俟夏秋。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized to transfer Green Standard troops and planned that in the first month of the coming year he would order Provincial Commander Sun Sike to Qinzhou and Zhao Liangdong to Fengxiang to join Zhang Yong and Wang Jinbao in a concerted advance; Zhang Yong and others said they must wait until summer and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai requested Green Standard reinforcements and planned to order Provincial Commander Sun Sike to Qinzhou and Zhao Liangdong to Fengxiang in the first month of the coming year for a joint advance with Zhang Yong and Wang Jinbao. Zhang Yong and the others insisted on waiting until summer and autumn.

sentences.zh: 上慮克漢中、興安轉餉難，令守諸要隘，分兵赴荊州攻三桂。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that supplying troops after taking Hanzhong and Xing'an would be difficult and ordered the garrison of key passes while detachments were sent to Jingzhou to attack Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the difficulty of supplying troops once Hanzhong and Xing'an were taken, the emperor ordered key passes held and detachments sent to Jingzhou against Sangui.

sentences.zh: 十六年，圖海招撫韓城等縣偽官，又遣兵逼禮縣、益門，先後敗賊五盤山、喬家山、塘坊廟、芭蕉園、沙窩諸處，复塔什堡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Tu Hai won over the false officials of Hancheng and other counties, sent troops against Li and Yimen, and in succession defeated rebels at Wupanshan, Qiaojiashan, Tangfangmiao, Bajiaoyuan, Shawo, and elsewhere, recovering Tashibao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Tu Hai won over puppet officials in Hancheng and other counties and sent troops against Li and Yimen. His forces defeated the rebels in turn at Wupanshan, Qiaojiashan, Tangfangmiao, Bajiaoyuan, Shawo, and other places, and recovered Tashibao.

sentences.zh: 十七年，复疏請分兵下漢中、興安，上密諭止之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again memorialized to divide forces and descend on Hanzhong and Xing'an; the emperor secretly ordered him to desist.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he again asked permission to divide his forces and take Hanzhong and Xing'an, but the emperor privately instructed him to hold back.

sentences.zh: 將軍佛尼勒等又敗賊牛頭山香泉，四川總督周有德亦敗賊秦嶺，复潼關堡五寨。

translations.literal: General Fonile and others again defeated rebels at Niutoushan Xiangquan; Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde also defeated rebels on the Qin Mountains and recovered the five stockades of Tongguan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: General Fonile and others again defeated the rebels at Niutoushan Xiangquan, while Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde routed them on the Qin Mountains and recovered the five stockades of Tongguan Fort.

sentences.zh: 慶陽賊袁本秀受三桂劄，謀亂。

translations.literal: The Qingyang rebel Yuan Benxiu received a commission from Sangui and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingyang rebel Yuan Benxiu received a commission from Sangui and plotted an uprising.

sentences.zh: 圖海發慶陽、宜君、延安三營兵，會王進寶討平之，斬本秀衛遠溝。

translations.literal: Tu Hai dispatched troops from the Qingyang, Yijun, and Yan'an camps, joined Wang Jinbao in suppressing the revolt, and beheaded Benxiu at Weiyuangou.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai sent troops from the Qingyang, Yijun, and Yan'an camps, joined Wang Jinbao in putting down the revolt, and beheaded Benxiu at Weiyuangou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，入覲。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he went to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 十八年，還鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 湖南、廣西平。

translations.literal: Hunan and Guangxi were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Guangxi were pacified.

sentences.zh: 上命亟攻寶雞，規取漢中、興安，定四川。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a swift attack on Baoji, planning to take Hanzhong and Xing'an and settle Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an immediate assault on Baoji, intending to seize Hanzhong and Xing'an and secure Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 圖海乃厲師攻益門鎮，破之。

translations.literal: Tu Hai then stiffened the army's discipline and attacked Yimen Town, which was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai tightened discipline and attacked Yimen Town, which fell.

sentences.zh: 會賊毀偏橋，兵不得進，狀聞，詔嚴責。

translations.literal: Just then the rebels destroyed the Pian Bridge so the army could not advance. When this was reported, an edict sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then destroyed Pian Bridge and blocked the advance. When Tu Hai reported this, the emperor issued a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 乃決策期分四路：圖海親率將軍佛尼勒等趨興安，總兵官程福亮為後援，屯舊縣關；

translations.literal: He then resolved on a timed advance in four columns: Tu Hai would personally lead General Fonile and others toward Xing'an, with Regional Commander Cheng Fuliang as rearguard stationed at Jiuxian Pass;
translations.idiomatic: He then planned a coordinated advance in four columns: Tu Hai would personally lead General Fonile and others toward Xing'an, with Regional Commander Cheng Fuliang in reserve at Jiuxian Pass;

sentences.zh: 將軍畢力克圖、提督孫思克等自略陽進，總兵官硃衣客為後援，駐西河；

translations.literal: General Biliketu and Provincial Commander Sun Sike would advance from Lueyang, with Regional Commander Zhu Yike as rearguard at Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: General Biliketu and Provincial Commander Sun Sike would advance from Lueyang, with Regional Commander Zhu Yike in reserve at Xihe;

sentences.zh: 將軍王進寶、總兵官費雅達自棧道進，總兵官高孟為後援，駐寶雞；

translations.literal: General Wang Jinbao and Regional Commander Fei Yada would advance by the plank road, with Regional Commander Gao Meng as rearguard at Baoji;
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Jinbao and Regional Commander Fei Yada would advance along the plank road, with Regional Commander Gao Meng in reserve at Baoji;

sentences.zh: 提督趙良棟自徽縣進。

translations.literal: Provincial Commander Zhao Liangdong would advance from Hui County.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commander Zhao Liangdong would advance from Hui County.

sentences.zh: 十月，師次鎮安，分兵為二隊，進敗三桂將王遇隆，渡乾玉河，奪梁河關。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army halted at Zhen'an, divided into two columns, advanced and defeated Sangui's general Wang Yulong, crossed the Qianyu River, and took Lianghe Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army halted at Zhen'an, split into two columns, defeated Sangui's general Wang Yulong, crossed the Qianyu River, and seized Lianghe Pass.

sentences.zh: 三桂將韓晉卿遁。

translations.literal: Sangui's general Han Jinqing fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's general Han Jinqing fled.

sentences.zh: 進寶亦復漢中。

translations.literal: Jinbao also recovered Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinbao also recovered Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 良棟复徽縣、略陽。

translations.literal: Liangdong recovered Hui County and Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong recovered Hui County and Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 畢力克圖復成縣，又復階州，遣參將康調元復文縣。

translations.literal: Biliketu recovered Cheng County and then Jiezhou, and sent Assistant Regional Commander Kang Tiaoyuan to recover Wen County.
translations.idiomatic: Biliketu recovered Cheng County and then Jiezhou, and dispatched Assistant Regional Commander Kang Tiaoyuan to recover Wen County.

sentences.zh: 於是平利、紫陽、石泉、漢陰、洵陽、白河、竹山、竹溪、上津諸縣皆下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pingli, Ziyang, Shiquan, Hanyin, Xunyang, Baihe, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Shangjin, and other counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pingli, Ziyang, Shiquan, Hanyin, Xunyang, Baihe, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Shangjin, and the other counties then fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 興安既克，圖海統大軍之半屯鳳翔，尋移漢中，護諸軍餉。

translations.literal: Once Xing'an was taken, Tu Hai commanded half the main army and encamped at Fengxiang, soon moving to Hanzhong to oversee supplies for all forces.
translations.idiomatic: After Xing'an fell, Tu Hai took half the main army to Fengxiang and soon moved to Hanzhong to oversee supplies for all the columns.

sentences.zh: 會降將譚洪复叛，陝西總督哈佔溯江討之，詔圖海遙為聲援。

translations.literal: Just then the surrendered general Tan Hong rebelled again. Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan pursued him upriver, and an edict ordered Tu Hai to lend distant support.
translations.idiomatic: About then the surrendered general Tan Hong rebelled again. Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan pursued him up the river, and the emperor ordered Tu Hai to lend distant support.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以疾徵還。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was recalled on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was recalled to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文襄。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 太宗實錄成，贈少保兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was posthumously given Junior Tutor with concurrent Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was posthumously made Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，追贈一等忠達公，配享太廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously advanced to first-rank Duke of Loyal Achievement and granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made first-rank Duke of Loyal Achievement and granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 子諾敏，襲爵，歷刑、禮二部尚書，正黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: His son Nuomin inherited the title, served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Rites, and was commander-in-chief of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nuomin inherited the title, served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Rites, and became commander-in-chief of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 諾敏子馬爾賽，自有傳。

translations.literal: Nuomin's son Ma'ersai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Nuomin's son Ma'ersai is the subject of a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 周昌初入城，自陳父明季死流寇，母孫剜目破面觸棺死，原捐軀表母烈。

translations.literal: When Zhou Chang first entered the city he declared that his father had died at the hands of bandits in the late Ming, and that his mother Sun had gouged out her eyes, mutilated her face, and dashed herself against the coffin to die; he wished to offer his life to honor her martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering the city, Zhou Chang explained that his father had been killed by bandits in the late Ming and that his mother Sun had gouged out her eyes, disfigured her face, and dashed herself against the coffin to die. He asked to give his own life in testimony to her martyrdom.

sentences.zh: 及輔臣降，圖海以聞。

translations.literal: When Fuchen had surrendered, Tu Hai reported it.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuchen surrendered, Tu Hai reported the fact to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命旌其母，遣官致祭，授昌布政使參政。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered honors for his mother, dispatched officials to perform sacrifices, and appointed Chang provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered honors for Chang's mother, sent officials to perform the sacrifices, and appointed Chang provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昌复參蔡毓榮軍事，事平，授山東登萊道，攝布政使，以與總兵互訐罷。

translations.literal: Chang again took part in Cai Yurong's military affairs; when affairs were settled he was made intendant of the Deng-Lai circuit in Shandong and acting provincial administration commissioner, but was dismissed for quarreling with the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chang again served on Cai Yurong's staff. When the campaign ended he was made intendant of the Deng-Lai circuit in Shandong and acting provincial administration commissioner, but was dismissed after quarreling with the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 昌既罷，猶喜言兵。

translations.literal: Though dismissed, Chang still delighted in speaking of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even after his dismissal, Chang still loved to talk of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹擾邊，數上書當事陳利害。

translations.literal: When Galdan harassed the frontier, he repeatedly wrote to those in authority setting forth advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: When Galdan raided the borderlands, he repeatedly wrote to those in power laying out the strategic stakes.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: He later died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 李之芳，字鄴園，山東武定人。

translations.literal: Li Zhifang, style name Yeyuan, was a native of Wuding in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhifang, whose style was Yeyuan, was a native of Wuding in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授金華府推官。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed reviewing official of Jinhua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed reviewing official of Jinhua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卓異，擢刑部主事。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding, he was promoted to principal in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in performance, he was promoted to principal in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，授廣西道御史。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to department director and was made investigating censor for the Guangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to department director and was appointed investigating censor for the Guangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏請革錢糧陋規，禁州縣官迎送。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish corrupt practices in tax collection and forbid prefectural and county officials from welcoming and escorting superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish corrupt practices in tax collection and to forbid prefectural and county officials from the elaborate welcoming and escorting of superiors.

sentences.zh: 十七年，巡按山西。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he toured as inspector of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he served as touring inspector of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，裁巡按，召回。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor acceded, the touring inspector posts were cut and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne, the touring inspector posts were abolished and he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi he asked for leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 二年，复授湖廣道御史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again appointed investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was again appointed investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，巡視浙江鹽政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he inspected salt administration in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he inspected salt administration in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 入掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He entered to direct affairs of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then put in charge of affairs for the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 大學士班布爾善坐鰲拜黨誅，之芳疏言：「昔大學士俱內直，諸司章奏，即日票擬。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed as a member of Oboi's faction. Zhifang memorialized: "Formerly all grand secretaries were on inner duty, and all documents from the ministries received draft responses the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed as a member of Oboi's faction. Zhifang memorialized: "In former times all grand secretaries served on inner duty, and memorials from the ministries received draft responses the same day.

sentences.zh: 自鰲拜輔政，大學士皆不入直，疏奏俱至次日看詳。

translations.literal: Since Oboi held power, no grand secretaries entered inner duty; memorials and reports were all reviewed only the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Since Oboi dominated the government, no grand secretaries entered inner duty, and memorials were not reviewed until the following day.

sentences.zh: 請復舊制，杜任意更改之弊。」

translations.literal: He asked to restore the old system and block the abuse of arbitrary changes."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the old system be restored to prevent arbitrary alterations."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「世祖時賞罰出至公，督撫不敢恣睢無忌。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Under the Shunzhi Emperor rewards and punishments issued from perfect impartiality, and governors-general dared not act wantonly without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Under the Shunzhi Emperor rewards and punishments issued from perfect impartiality, and governors-general did not dare act with reckless impunity.

sentences.zh: 十八年以後，督撫率多夤緣而得，有恃無恐。

translations.literal: After the eighteenth year most governors-general obtained their posts through patronage and acted without fear.
translations.idiomatic: After the eighteenth year most governors-general obtained their posts through patronage and acted without fear of consequences.

sentences.zh: 勒索屬員，擾害百姓。

translations.literal: They extorted from subordinates and harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: They extorted their subordinates and harassed the common people.

sentences.zh: 夫直省億萬之眾，皆世祖留遺之群黎，我皇上愛養之赤子，何堪此輩朘削？

translations.literal: The hundreds of millions in the provinces are all the masses the late emperor bequeathed and children whom our present emperor nourishes—how can they bear such exploitation?
translations.idiomatic: The hundreds of millions in the provinces are the people the late emperor bequeathed and the children our present emperor nourishes—how can they endure such exploitation?

sentences.zh: 自與受同罪之法嚴，與者不承，則言者即涉虛，非特不敢糾督撫，且不敢糾司道守令。

translations.literal: With the law that giver and taker share guilt strictly applied, if the taker does not confess, the accuser is deemed false—so not only do they dare not impeach governors-general, they dare not impeach circuit intendants, prefects, and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Because the law that punishes both giver and taker alike is strictly enforced, if the taker does not confess the accuser is deemed to have lied—so men dare not impeach governors-general, and dare not even impeach circuit intendants, prefects, or magistrates.

sentences.zh: 有貪之利，無貪之害，又何憚而不怙惡自恣？

translations.literal: With gain in corruption and no harm, why would they not persist in evil without restraint?
translations.idiomatic: When corruption brings profit and no penalty, why should they not cling to evil and act as they please?

sentences.zh: 今皇上親政，乞親裁，罷黜溺職督撫，以肅吏治。」

translations.literal: Now that the emperor has taken power in person, he begged that the emperor personally decide and dismiss negligent governors-general to rectify official conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has taken power in person, he begged that you personally decide the matter, dismiss negligent governors-general, and restore discipline among officials."

sentences.zh: 疏下部，尋甄別各省督撫，黜其尤者數人。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries; soon governors-general in each province were screened and several of the worst were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the ministries, and before long governors-general throughout the provinces were screened and several of the worst offenders were removed.

sentences.zh: 進秩視四品，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to fourth-grade equivalent and made left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in rank to the equivalent of fourth grade and appointed left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 之芳數上封事，請嚴巡鹽考績，慎外官罰俸，皆關治體。

translations.literal: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials asking for strict inspection of salt patrol performance and careful application of fines to outside officials—all concerned fundamentals of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials calling for strict evaluation of salt patrols and careful use of salary fines against field officials—measures that all touched the foundations of good government.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以兵部侍郎總督浙江軍務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, as vice minister of war he was made commander-in-chief of Zhejiang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while serving as vice minister of war, he was made commander-in-chief of Zhejiang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 會吳三桂反，十三年，奏請復標兵原額，督習槍砲。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year he memorialized to restore the original establishment of garrison troops and supervise drill in firearms.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, he memorialized in the thirteenth year to restore the garrison troops to their original strength and to supervise training in firearms.

sentences.zh: 疏甫上，耿精忠亦叛，遣其將曾養性、白顯忠、馬九玉數道闚浙，浙大震。

translations.literal: Just as the memorial was submitted, Geng Jingzhong also rebelled and sent his generals Zeng Yangxing, Bai Xianzhong, and Ma Jiuyu in several columns to threaten Zhejiang; Zhejiang was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the memorial been submitted when Geng Jingzhong rebelled as well, sending his generals Zeng Yangxing, Bai Xianzhong, and Ma Jiuyu in several columns to threaten Zhejiang. The province was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 之芳檄諸將扼仙霞關，調總兵李榮率副將王廷梅、牟大寅、陳世凱、鮑虎等分道禦寇。

translations.literal: Zhifang ordered generals to hold Xianxia Pass and directed Regional Commander Li Rong with deputy generals Wang Tingmei, Mou Dayin, Chen Shikai, Bao Hu, and others to oppose the enemy on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang ordered his generals to hold Xianxia Pass and directed Regional Commander Li Rong, with deputy generals Wang Tingmei, Mou Dayin, Chen Shikai, Bao Hu, and others, to oppose the enemy on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 時上命都統賴塔率師入浙，五月，偕賴塔率滿洲兵千、綠旗兵二千、鄉勇五百，進駐衢州。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor ordered Banner Commander-in-Chief Laita to lead troops into Zhejiang. In the fifth month Zhifang joined Laita with a thousand Manchu troops, two thousand Green Standard troops, and five hundred militia, advancing to garrison at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered Banner Commander-in-Chief Laita to lead troops into Zhejiang. In the fifth month Zhifang joined him with a thousand Manchu troops, two thousand Green Standard troops, and five hundred militia, and advanced to garrison Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾皆謂會城重地，不宜輕委。

translations.literal: All said the provincial capital was an important place and should not be lightly entrusted elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said the provincial capital was too important to leave lightly defended.

sentences.zh: 之芳曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 衢踞上游，無衢，是無浙也。

translations.literal: Quzhou stands on the upper reaches; without Quzhou there is no Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou commands the upper reaches; without Quzhou there is no Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，義無反顧。」

translations.literal: In today's affair there is no turning back."
translations.idiomatic: In today's fight there is no turning back."

sentences.zh: 顯忠自常山陷開化、壽昌、淳安，養性自處州犯義烏、浦江、東陽、湯溪，沿河阻餉道。

translations.literal: Xianzhong from Changshan took Kaihua, Shouchang, and Chun'an; Yangxing from Chuzhou attacked Yiwu, Pujiang, Dongyang, and Tangxi, blocking supply routes along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong advanced from Changshan and took Kaihua, Shouchang, and Chun'an; Yangxing advanced from Chuzhou against Yiwu, Pujiang, Dongyang, and Tangxi, blocking supply routes along the river.

sentences.zh: 溫州鎮總兵祖弘勳叛，召寇陷平陽，再進陷黃岩，集悍卒數万窺衢州。

translations.literal: Wenzhou garrison commander Zu Hongxun rebelled, summoned the enemy, and took Pingyang, then advanced and took Huangyan, gathering tens of thousands of fierce troops to threaten Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou garrison commander Zu Hongxun rebelled, called in the enemy, and seized Pingyang, then advanced and took Huangyan, gathering tens of thousands of fierce troops to threaten Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，之芳與賴塔閱兵水亭門，率總兵官李榮、副都統瑚圖等薄賊壘，軍坑西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zhifang and Laita reviewed troops at the Water Pavilion Gate, led Regional Commander Li Rong, Vice Commander-in-Chief Hutu, and others to press the rebel camp at Junkeng West.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhifang and Laita reviewed the troops at the Water Pavilion Gate, then led Regional Commander Li Rong, Vice Commander-in-Chief Hutu, and others to assault the rebel camp west of Junkeng.

sentences.zh: 之芳手執刀督陣，或請少避，之芳曰：「三軍司命在吾，退即為賊乘。

translations.literal: Zhifang held a blade himself to supervise the battle formation. When someone asked him to withdraw slightly, Zhifang said: "The fate of the whole army rests with me; if we retreat the enemy will seize the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang took a blade in hand to direct the battle line. When someone urged him to withdraw a little, he said, "The fate of the whole army rests with me; if we fall back the enemy will seize the advantage.

sentences.zh: 今日勝敗，即吾死生矣！」

translations.literal: Today's victory or defeat is my life or death!"
translations.idiomatic: Today's victory or defeat is my life or death!"

sentences.zh: 守備程龍怯戰，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Cheng Long fought timidly and was beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Cheng Long fought timidly and was beheaded as an example to the troops.

sentences.zh: 麾眾越壕拔柵，敗之。

translations.literal: He directed the troops over the moat and pulled down the palisade, defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men over the moat, tore down the palisade, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遣陳世凱乘勝复義烏、湯​​溪，鮑虎复壽昌、淳安，牟大寅破常山，王廷梅敗賊於金華石梁、大溝源，李榮亦復東陽，复敗賊於金華壽溪，馘賊將，毀寨十八。

translations.literal: He sent Chen Shikai to follow up the victory and recover Yiwu and Tangxi; Bao Hu recovered Shouchang and Chun'an; Mou Dayin broke Changshan; Wang Tingmei defeated rebels at Shiliang and Dagouyuan in Jinhua; Li Rong also recovered Dongyang and again defeated rebels at Shouxi in Jinhua, beheading a rebel general and destroying eighteen stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Shikai to press the victory and recover Yiwu and Tangxi; Bao Hu recovered Shouchang and Chun'an; Mou Dayin broke Changshan; Wang Tingmei defeated the rebels at Shiliang and Dagouyuan in Jinhua; Li Rong recovered Dongyang and again routed the rebels at Shouxi in Jinhua, beheading a rebel general and destroying eighteen stockades.

sentences.zh: 參將洪起元復嵊縣。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Hong Qiyuan recovered Sheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Regional Commander Hong Qiyuan recovered Sheng County.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之芳調度有方。

translations.literal: An edict praised Zhifang's effective overall direction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Zhifang for his skillful overall direction of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊將桑明等五萬眾由常山逼衢州西溝溪，倚山為營，覬聯南路賊巢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebel general Sang Ming and fifty thousand men from Changshan pressed Xigouxi west of Quzhou, made camps against the mountain, and sought to link with southern rebel nests.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebel general Sang Ming led fifty thousand men from Changshan against Xigouxi west of Quzhou, pitched camps along the mountainside, and sought to link up with rebel strongholds to the south.

sentences.zh: 之芳與賴塔議，出不意，遣廷梅與參領禪布夜趨溝溪，分隊進攻，又大破之，賊棄營遁。

translations.literal: Zhifang and Laita agreed to strike unexpectedly, sent Tingmei and Battalion Leader Chanbu by night to Xigouxi, divided into columns to attack, and again routed them; the rebels abandoned camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang and Laita agreed on a surprise attack, sent Tingmei and Battalion Leader Chanbu by night to Xigouxi, divided into columns, and routed the enemy again; the rebels abandoned their camps and fled.

sentences.zh: 十四年，康親王杰書破曾養性金華，复處州；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Prince Kang Jieshu broke Zeng Yangxing at Jinhua and recovered Chuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Prince Kang Jieshu defeated Zeng Yangxing at Jinhua and recovered Chuzhou;

sentences.zh: 貝子傅拉塔亦復黃岩，進圍溫州。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Lalta also recovered Huangyan and advanced to besiege Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Lalta also recovered Huangyan and advanced to besiege Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟九玉踞江山、常山、開化，連寨數十，與之芳相持。

translations.literal: Only Jiuyu held Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua with dozens of linked stockades, locked in stalemate with Zhifang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jiuyu still held Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua behind dozens of linked stockades, locked in stalemate with Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 五月，乘大雨河溢，由南塘搗賊前嶺，陣斬七百餘級。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, taking advantage of heavy rain and flooded rivers, they struck the rebel forward ridge from Nantang, killing more than seven hundred in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, exploiting heavy rain and flooded rivers, they struck the rebel forward ridge from Nantang and killed more than seven hundred in battle.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遣將自遂安連破賊寨，遂復開化。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he sent generals from Sui'an to break rebel stockades in succession and recovered Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he sent generals from Sui'an to break rebel stockades one after another and recovered Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 會鄭錦入漳、泉，耿繼祚方攻建昌潰營遁。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jing entered Zhang and Quan, Geng Jizuo was attacking Jianchang when his camp collapsed and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing invaded Zhang and Quan, Geng Jizuo was attacking Jianchang when his camp collapsed and he fled.

sentences.zh: 上知閩中有變，命王撤溫州之圍取福建，之芳乃建議直搗仙霞關，曰：「進取之路，不在溫、處而在衢。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of disorders in Fujian and ordered the prince to lift the Wenzhou siege and take Fujian. Zhifang then proposed to strike directly at Xianxia Pass, saying: "The path of advance lies not in Wen and Chu but in Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of disorders in Fujian, the emperor ordered the prince to lift the siege of Wenzhou and take Fujian. Zhifang then proposed striking directly at Xianxia Pass, saying, "The road of advance lies not through Wen and Chu but through Qu.

sentences.zh: 雖九玉死守河西難猝破，然其南江山，西則常山，皆間道可襲。

translations.literal: Though Jiuyu stubbornly held the west bank of the river and could not be taken quickly, Jiangshan lay to his south and Changshan to his west—both were paths that could be raided.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiuyu stubbornly held the west bank of the river and could not be taken quickly, Jiangshan lies to his south and Changshan to his west—both are paths that can be struck.

sentences.zh: 我兵一進，使彼首尾受敵，即河西之壘不能獨完。」

translations.literal: If our troops advance once, he will be caught fore and aft and even the west-bank stockades cannot hold alone."
translations.idiomatic: Once our troops advance, he will be caught between two fires and even the stockades on the west bank cannot hold by themselves."

sentences.zh: 王至衢州，從之芳議。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Quzhou he followed Zhifang's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Quzhou he adopted Zhifang's plan.

sentences.zh: 遂進兵大溪灘，复江山，九玉走，欲別取道奪仙霞。

translations.literal: They advanced to Daxitan, recovered Jiangshan; Jiuyu fled, intending to take another route and seize Xianxia.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Daxitan and recovered Jiangshan. Jiuyu fled, intending to take another route and seize Xianxia Pass.

sentences.zh: 諸將受之芳密檄，急據關夾擊，其將金應虎等窮蹙降。

translations.literal: Generals received Zhifang's secret dispatch and hastened to hold the pass for a pincer attack; his generals Jin Yinghu and others, cornered, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The generals received Zhifang's secret orders, rushed to hold the pass, and caught the enemy in a pincer; Jin Yinghu and other rebel commanders, cornered, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王師下福建，臨行，之芳啟曰：「王但飭諸軍勿虜掠，即長驅入，兵可不血刃也。」

translations.literal: As the imperial army descended on Fujian, on departure Zhifang submitted: "Your Highness need only forbid the armies from looting, and you may advance at full speed without drawing a sword."
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial army marched into Fujian, Zhifang submitted on the eve of departure: "Your Highness need only forbid looting, and you may advance at full speed without drawing a sword."

sentences.zh: 未幾精忠降，溫、處賊皆潰散。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhong surrendered and rebels in Wen and Chu all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jingzhong surrendered and the rebels in Wen and Chu all dispersed.

sentences.zh: 精忠所署置總兵馬鵬、汪文生、陳山，將軍程鳳等猶踞玉山、鉛山、弋陽、德興，之芳請會剿。

translations.literal: Regional commanders Ma Peng, Wang Wensheng, and Chen Shan and General Cheng Feng, whom Jingzhong had appointed, still held Yushan, Qianshan, Yiyang, and Dexing. Zhifang asked for a joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders Ma Peng, Wang Wensheng, and Chen Shan and General Cheng Feng, whom Jingzhong had appointed, still held Yushan, Qianshan, Yiyang, and Dexing. Zhifang requested a joint campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂兵寇吉安、袁州，江西兵不能東，乃獨遣兵复玉山，文生遁；

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui's troops threatened Ji'an and Yuanzhou; Jiangxi troops could not move east, so he sent troops alone to recover Yushan and Wensheng fled;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Sangui's troops threatened Ji'an and Yuanzhou, and Jiangxi's forces could not move east. Zhifang therefore sent troops on his own to recover Yushan, and Wensheng fled;

sentences.zh: 自白沙關趨德興，擒鵬；

translations.literal: from Baishaguan he pressed toward Dexing and captured Peng;
translations.idiomatic: from Baishaguan he pressed toward Dexing and captured Peng;

sentences.zh: 遣游擊郭守金等復鉛山、興安、弋陽、貴溪諸縣。

translations.literal: he sent guerrilla officer Guo Shoujin and others to recover Qianshan, Xing'an, Yiyang, Guixi, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: he sent guerrilla officer Guo Shoujin and others to recover Qianshan, Xing'an, Yiyang, Guixi, and the other counties.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之芳勦賊鄰省有功，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Zhifang's meritorious suppression of rebels in a neighboring province and added the title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Zhifang's meritorious suppression of rebels in a neighboring province and granted him the title of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣參將蔣懋勳等敗賊玉山椒岩，山降。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he sent Assistant Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun and others to defeat rebels at Jiaoyan in Yushan; Shan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he sent Assistant Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun and others to defeat the rebels at Jiaoyan in Yushan, and Chen Shan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 先是文生、鳳皆乞降，而鳳病死，其妻王玉貞籍所屬六萬八千餘人就撫，而精忠將林爾瞻猶擁眾石壟。

translations.literal: Earlier Wensheng and Feng had both asked to surrender, but Feng died of illness; his wife Wang Yuzhen registered more than sixty-eight thousand followers for pacification, while Jingzhong's general Lin Erzhan still held a crowd at Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wensheng and Feng had both asked to surrender, but Feng died of illness. His wife Wang Yuzhen registered more than sixty-eight thousand followers for pacification, while Jingzhong's general Lin Erzhan still held a force at Shilong.

sentences.zh: 之芳令懋勳等扼要隘，自以數十騎入寨，往撫慰之，爾瞻乃降。

translations.literal: Zhifang ordered Maoxun and others to block key passes; he himself entered the stockade with several dozen horsemen to console them, and Erzhan then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang ordered Maoxun and others to block the key passes, then entered the stockade himself with several dozen horsemen to reassure them, and Erzhan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擊賊子午口，克八仙、老鼠諸洞，賊寨悉平。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they attacked the rebel stronghold Ziwukou, took the caves of Baxian and Laoshu, and all rebel stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year they attacked the rebel stronghold at Ziwukou, took the caves of Baxian and Laoshu, and pacified all the rebel stockades.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦寇瀕海，遣將嚴守禦，敗之於廟嶺湖，又敗之於溫州。

translations.literal: Zheng Jing raided the coast; Zhifang sent generals to guard strictly, defeating him at Miaoling Lake and again at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing raided the coast. Zhifang sent generals to guard the approaches strictly, defeating him at Miaoling Lake and again at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦將詹天樞詣世凱降。

translations.literal: Zheng's general Zhan Tianshu came to Chen Shikai to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's general Zhan Tianshu came to Chen Shikai to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十八年，檄定海總兵牟大寅斬錦將童耀等孝順洋，奪獲船隻、器械以還。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he ordered Dinghai garrison commander Mou Dayin to behead Zheng's general Tong Yao and others at Xiaoshunyang, seizing ships and weapons on the return.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he ordered Dinghai garrison commander Mou Dayin to behead Zheng's general Tong Yao and others at Xiaoshunyang and return with captured ships and weapons.

sentences.zh: 之芳練世故，沉幾善謀。

translations.literal: Zhifang was seasoned in worldly affairs, deliberate and skilled in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang was seasoned in worldly affairs, deliberate in judgment, and skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 康親王師將行，問之芳：「所策固萬全乎？」

translations.literal: When Prince Kang's army was about to march, he asked Zhifang: "Is your plan completely secure?"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang's army was about to march, he asked Zhifang, "Is your plan completely secure?"

sentences.zh: 之芳曰：「軍已發，猶豫則士氣沮。」

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "The army has already set out; hesitation will sap morale."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang replied, "The army has already set out; hesitation will sap morale."

sentences.zh: 乃詣王曰：「虜在吾目中久，明日捷書至矣！」

translations.literal: He then said to the prince: "The enemy has long been in my sight; tomorrow the victory report will arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: He then said to the prince, "I have had the enemy in my sights for some time; tomorrow the victory report will arrive!"

sentences.zh: 前軍捷書果至，傑書大喜，以為神。

translations.literal: The advance army's victory report indeed arrived; Jieshu was overjoyed and thought it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The advance army's victory report indeed arrived the next day; Jieshu was overjoyed and thought it miraculous.

sentences.zh: 在杭州，與將軍圖喇約為兄弟。

translations.literal: At Hangzhou he swore brotherhood with General Tula.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou he swore brotherhood with General Tula.

sentences.zh: 精忠既叛，語圖喇勿縱兵暴民。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong rebelled he told Tula not to let the troops abuse the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong rebelled he urged Tula not to let the troops abuse the people.

sentences.zh: 有滿兵犯法，之芳縛詣圖喇，以軍法治之，一軍肅然。

translations.literal: When a Manchu soldier broke the law, Zhifang bound him and brought him to Tula to punish by military law; the whole army was awed into discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When a Manchu soldier broke the law, Zhifang bound him and brought him before Tula for punishment under military law, and the whole army fell into strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 浙亂平，疏請蠲被兵州縣額賦，安輯流亡，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When the Zhejiang disorders were pacified he memorialized to remit tax quotas of war-stricken prefectures and counties and settle the displaced, winning great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When the disorders in Zhejiang were pacified he memorialized to remit tax quotas in war-stricken prefectures and counties and to settle displaced people, winning great respect and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 所拔偏裨，皆累功至方鎮，而之芳以督臣不敘。

translations.literal: The subordinate officers he promoted all rose through merit to regional commands, yet Zhifang as governor received no account of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate officers he promoted all rose through repeated merit to regional commands, yet Zhifang himself, as governor, received no credit in the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 久之，追論大溪灘破賊功，授拖沙喇哈番，準襲一次。

translations.literal: After a long time his achievement in defeating rebels at Daxitan was reviewed; he was granted tosara hašan, inheritable once.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward his achievement in defeating the rebels at Daxitan was reviewed and he was granted tosara hašan, inheritable once.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of War and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of War and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was made grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，御史郭琇疏劾大學士明珠，謂內閣票擬，皆聽明珠指揮，上既罷明珠，並命之芳休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Censor Guo Xiu memorialized to impeach Grand Secretary Mingzhu, saying all draft responses in the Grand Secretariat followed Mingzhu's command. The emperor had already dismissed Mingzhu and also ordered Zhifang to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Censor Guo Xiu memorialized to impeach Grand Secretary Mingzhu, charging that all draft responses in the Grand Secretariat followed Mingzhu's orders. The emperor had already dismissed Mingzhu and also ordered Zhifang to retire.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒於家，諡文襄。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died at home, posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he died at home and was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 之芳既卒，聖祖思其功，嘗諭群臣曰：「人能效命，即為勇士。

translations.literal: After Zhifang's death the Kangxi Emperor thought of his achievements and once told the ministers: "One who gives his life in service is a brave man.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhifang's death the Kangxi Emperor recalled his achievements and once told his ministers, "A man who stakes his life in service is a true warrior.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠叛，時之芳為總督，雖不諳騎射，執刀立船首，率眾突前破敵。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Zhifang was governor; though unskilled in riding and archery, he held a blade at the bow of the boat and led the men in a frontal assault that broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Zhifang was governor. Though unskilled in riding and archery, he stood at the bow with a blade in hand and led his men in a frontal charge that broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼時同出征者，還京皆稱其勇。

translations.literal: Those who campaigned with him at the time all praised his bravery on return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had campaigned with him all praised his bravery on their return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 今承平久，善射，能約束士卒，尚不乏人。

translations.literal: Now in long peace those skilled in archery who can discipline troops are still not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In these long years of peace, men skilled in archery who can discipline troops are still not hard to find.

sentences.zh: 若屢經戰陣者，甚難得也！」

translations.literal: But those who have repeatedly seen battle are very hard to find!"
translations.idiomatic: But men who have repeatedly seen battle are very hard to find!"

sentences.zh: 世宗命立賢良祠，諭曰：「德若湯斌、功若之芳者，祀之。」

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthy Officials erected and said: "Enshrine those whose virtue is like Tang Bin's and whose achievement is like Zhifang's."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthy Officials built and instructed, "Enshrine those whose virtue is like Tang Bin's and whose achievement is like Zhifang's."

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，錄勳臣後，命予恩騎尉，世襲。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, when recording descendants of meritorious officials, his line was granted Enjiwei, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign, when recording descendants of meritorious officials, his line was granted the Enjiwei rank, inheritable in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 論曰：圖海始阻撤籓之議，及其鷹揚西土，綏靖秦隴，卒收底川之績。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tu Hai at first opposed the proposal to withdraw the feudatories; later he soared in the west, pacified Qin and Long, and at last won the achievement of settling Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Tu Hai had first opposed withdrawing the feudatories; later he took the field in the west with eagle vigor, pacified Qin and Long, and in the end secured the achievement of settling Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川軍入滇，遂竟全功。

translations.literal: When the Sichuan army entered Yunnan, the full victory was at last completed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Sichuan army entered Yunnan, the great enterprise was brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 之芳力扼三衢，敵雖東略，終不能得志仙霞。

translations.literal: Zhifang strove to hold the three Qu prefectures; though the enemy raided eastward, they could never prevail at Xianxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang strove to hold the three Qu prefectures; though the enemy thrust eastward, they never gained their aim at Xianxia Pass.

sentences.zh: 下閩之功，與有勞焉。

translations.literal: In the merit of subduing Fujian, he too had a share of labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Fujian, too, he had a share of the achievement.

sentences.zh: 雖曰遭時盤錯，抑亦聖祖馭材之效哉？

translations.literal: Though one may say they encountered a tangled age, was it not also the effect of the sage emperor's employment of talent?
translations.idiomatic: One may say they lived in a tangled age, yet was it not also the fruit of the sage emperor's skill in employing men?

sentences.zh: 並踐綸輔，易名曰襄。

translations.literal: Both reached the rank of grand councilor and took the posthumous character Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Both rose to grand councilor and received the posthumous character Xiang in their titles.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，偉矣！

translations.literal: Alas, how great they were!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how great they were!
